name: manual_ad340c
claim: Redirect-following is a SEPARATE control surface from URL/DNS validation, and every HTTP library/SDK encountered this session defaulted to following redirects silently: urllib.request (HTTPRedirectHandler installed by default), and the openai SDK's own httpx client (follow_redirects=True, NOT httpx.Client's own False default -- SDKs commonly override library defaults for convenience). Validating a request's INITIAL url/host is not a redirect defense -- a validated, trusted target can still redirect the SAME request anywhere, and the transport will follow it with zero re-validation unless redirect-following is explicitly disabled or intercepted. This pattern recurred four distinct times in one session, each independently discovered, each a real gap: (1) ssrf_pinned_adapter.py's OWN max_redirects=0 accidentally broke its own redirect-revalidation loop via requests.Session's internal precomputation quirk (over-correction: blocked its own legitimate redirect handling); (2) the adapter's redirect-denial test false-passed via hop-limit exhaustion, never actually proving a metadata redirect was rejected; (3) perplexity_client.py's openai-SDK-backed client silently auto-followed redirects from api.perplexity.ai with zero revalidation (under-correction: no redirect defense at all); (4) autoresearch_bridge.py's LM Studio probe validated the initial URL then silently auto-followed any redirect via urllib's default opener (same under-correction, different library). General rule for future wiring: for ANY new outbound HTTP client (new library, new SDK, new vendor integration), explicitly verify and set its redirect-following behavior -- do not assume url/DNS validation covers it, do not assume the library's own documented default matches what the SDK actually constructs, and write a test that PROVES a redirect to a denied target is refused (not a test that merely exercises a code path that happens to also deny it via a different mechanism, like a hop-count limit).
conditions: SDK http client default differs from library default
recurring pattern across ssrf_pinned_adapter perplexity_client autoresearch_bridge
verify redirect refused not just any denial

decisions.notes: Discovered while implementing PT-T5-API-005-adjacent Layer-2 wiring for PT-endpoint-hardening-checklists.md's PR-P3 (perplexity_client.py, autoresearch_bridge.py) on 2026-08-22. Each of the four instances was found independently across this session (two while fixing ssrf_pinned_adapter.py's own bugs earlier, two while wiring the two remaining PR-P3 clients just now) -- writing this as a single connected pattern rather than four separate atomic lessons because the underlying mechanism (assume-safe-because-validated, redirect defaults silently override that assumption) is the same root cause every time, and a future agent hitting instance #5 in a new file should recognize it from this pattern description, not have to independently rediscover the class of bug a fifth time.
